notes: Hard (total 11). Offline provisioning of an R Jupyter kernel plus the R graph/data-frame packages for causal work. The environment ships R + jupyter tooling but NO IRkernel/jsonlite/data.table: they exist only as vendored .debs under /app/vendor that the agent must install offline (apt/dpkg against local artifacts, resolving dependency ordering), then register a user-level kernelspec with the exact name/displayname from /app/workbench.conf via IRkernel::installspec, and satisfy a kernelspec-integrity invariant (every listed kernelspec has an existing executable argv[0]) by removing a stale broken legacy-r kernelspec — an environment-repair sub-problem with a distinct failure signature (debugging_ambiguity=2). dependent_stages=2 (deb install -> IRkernel importable -> kernelspec registered -> notebooks executable). Deliverables: an idempotent /app/provision.sh (run twice by the verifier; interaction_statefulness=1) and a live /app/workbench_report.json derived from the environment (kernel, argv[0] r_binary, loaded packages, exact R major.minor string; quantitative_correctness=1). The verifier independently re-checks package loading via Rscript, parses jupyter kernelspec list --json, and EXECUTES the visible notebook plus three hidden data.table/jsonlite notebooks through the registered rcw kernel via nbconvert (hidden_case_generalization=1, tool_breadth=2: apt/dpkg, R/IRkernel, jupyter/nbconvert). Distinct from the sibling kernel task: offline vendored-deb install, integrity invariant over ALL kernelspecs, exact-name conf-driven registration, and kernel-execution probes instead of static existence checks.
